Residential Demolition

The knockdown half of a knockdown rebuild

Full house demolition for knockdown rebuilds, duplex sites and new development. The house comes down, the asbestos is dealt with properly first, and the block is handed back at a level your builder can start on.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything comes down

Six things have to be done first, and not all of them are ours

Most knockdowns that run late run late on this list rather than on the machine work. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Hazardous materials survey

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    A sample based survey of everything that will be disturbed. On a pre 1990 house this is not optional.

  2. 02

    Demolition approval

    Who You or your builder, through council or a private certifier

    A complying development certificate or a development consent, depending on the property.

  3. 03

    Service disconnections

    Who You, with each authority

    Power, water, gas and sewer. These have the longest lead time of anything on the list and they are not ours to book.

  4. 04

    Asbestos removal and clearance

    Who Licensed asbestos removalist, then an independent assessor

    Removal under the control measures the material requires, then air monitoring and a clearance certificate.

  5. 05

    SafeWork notification

    Who Max

    Lodged where the work requires it, with the notice period the regulation sets.

  6. 06

    Site protection

    Who Max

    Fencing, hoarding where it is needed, dust and sediment control, and protection of the adjoining property.

On the day

What actually happens once we are on site

By the time a machine arrives the house is already empty, disconnected and cleared of asbestos. What is left is the structure, and it comes apart in an order rather than all at once.

  • Soft strip. Anything that is not structure and not already removed: fit out, linings, fixtures, floor coverings.
  • Roof and upper structure. Taken down with a grapple rather than pushed, so material lands where it can be sorted instead of across the block.
  • Walls and frame. Worked down in sections, with the adjoining boundary watched the whole way.
  • Load out. Separated material leaves on different trucks to different destinations as it is generated, not stockpiled.
  • Slab and footings, if included. Broken out, with the clean concrete going to recycling rather than landfill.
  • Grade and hand back. Levelled to what your engineer specified, swept, and the dockets handed over.

Asbestos is handled before the machine arrives

We manage the whole pathway as part of the contract. The removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and the clearance certificate is issued independently. Max holds the demolition licence, not the asbestos removal licence.

Before you book

What homeowners and builders ask us first

What does a house demolition cost?
The honest answer is that it depends on four things, and anyone quoting before they know them is guessing. Those are the size and construction of the house, how much of it is asbestos, what machine can physically get onto the block, and whether the slab, footings and driveway are coming out as well. We attend the site, look at all four, and give you a number that holds.
Is the slab included?
Only if you ask for it. Removing the slab, the footings, the driveway and the paths is extra machine time and a lot more cartage, so it is quoted as its own line. Most knockdown rebuilds do take it out, because the new design rarely sits exactly where the old one did. Ask your builder what the engineer needs and tell us.
How long before we can start the new build?
The demolition itself is usually a few days. The things that decide your start date are the approval, the disconnections and the asbestos clearance, and those are measured in weeks. Start them the day you have approval rather than the week before you want us on site.
What about the trees and the pool?
Both can come out with the house and both are separate scopes. A pool is an excavation job as much as a demolition one, because the shell has to come out and the hole has to be backfilled and compacted properly or your new slab will find the soft spot later.
Do you deal with the neighbours?
We protect the adjoining property, brace anything that needs it and keep the dust down. Telling the neighbours what is about to happen is worth doing, and we will give you the dates so you can.
What is left when you finish?
A cleared, graded block at the level your engineer specified, swept, with the fencing still up if you want it, and the disposal dockets handed over.
